text: {"claims":[{"cid":"c1","text":"Standard competitive models predict that a binding wage floor above equilibrium reduces the labour employers demand, causing job losses.","cited_pids":["min_wage#0"]},{"cid":"c2","text":"Some regional studies found falls in teen and low-skill employment after sharp minimum wage increases.","cited_pids":["min_wage#3"]},{"cid":"c3","text":"Studies of large local minimum wage rises report reduced scheduled hours for low-wage workers.","cited_pids":["min_wage#1"]},{"cid":"c4","text":"Employers in low-margin sectors may respond to higher minimum wages by automating and cutting entry-level positions.","cited_pids":["min_wage#2"]},{"cid":"c5","text":"The Card and Krueger fast food study found no employment decline in New Jersey after its minimum wage increase.","cited_pids":["min_wage#4"]},{"cid":"c6","text":"Monopsony models suggest a moderate minimum wage floor can raise both wages and employment.","cited_pids":["min_wage#5"]},{"cid":"c7","text":"A meta-analysis finds minimum wage employment effects clustered near zero, with publication bias inflating negative findings.","cited_pids":["min_wage#6"]},{"cid":"c8","text":"Some observed firms kept headcount broadly unchanged after minimum wage rises because lower turnover offset higher labour costs.","cited_pids":["min_wage#7"]},{"cid":"c9","text":"On balance, minimum wage employment effects are small on average but can be negative in some settings.","cited_pids":[]},{"cid":"c10","text":"The size of the wage increase and the structure of the labour market determine whether employment effects are negative.","cited_pids":[]}]}
